overall_summary: Space-themed anomalies and extreme cosmic physics are the clear growth drivers for FACTVERSE, with the latest space upload ('The Planet of Burning Ice') rapidly becoming the top-performing video. Conversely, abstract psychology and brain-fact videos consistently underperform, struggling to capture initial viewer interest.

winning_patterns.evidence: 'The Planet of Burning Ice' (678 views, 8 likes), 'The Largest Ocean in Space' (460 views, 5 likes), and 'What Does Outer Space Actually Smell Like?' (368 views, 4 likes) represent the channel's highest-performing tier.
winning_patterns.action: Produce highly visual, sensory-focused space content (extreme temperatures, smells, tastes, and weather in space) using high-contrast cosmic imagery.

winning_patterns.evidence: 'Sharks Are Older Than Trees?' (302 views) and 'This Animal Literally Dies Every Winter!' (179 views) maintain strong baseline viewership compared to other non-space topics.
winning_patterns.action: Create content comparing biological timelines or extreme animal survival mechanisms that defy common sense.

weak_patterns.evidence: 'Your Brain Can Create Fake Memories' (5 views and 54 views across uploads) and 'The Real Reason Songs Get Stuck In Your Head' (17 views) consistently fail to gain traction.
weak_patterns.action: Avoid passive, explanatory psychology facts. If exploring the mind, pivot to interactive 'test your brain' styles that force viewer participation.

next_video.reason: Aligns with the top-performing 16-second format and leverages the highly successful 'extreme planetary weather' theme established by the burning ice and glass rain concepts.

experiment: Test an interactive 'optical illusion' or 'brain test' Short to see if active viewer participation can rescue the underperforming psychology category.
